ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Egypt's EMLCU internal terrorism and Money Laundering watch-list. Consent of the CBE-licensed bank is required before opening the company's Swift TT / Airwallex payment rails; CDD/EDD measures are applied under Egypt's National Risk Assessment (NRA) framework. Continuous re-screening at onboarding, at every government filing benchmark, and on an ongoing risk-based schedule not exceeding 90 days; results recorded in the EMLCU-prescribed PEP and sanctions register. Given the Low_Risk_Standard banking tier, the institution shall nevertheless perform Source-of-Funds attestation for each equity contribution above USD 10,000, and any governmental or state-owned counterparty will trigger Enhanced Due Diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Foreign Trade (GAFI) Investor Center / 'Invest in Egypt' digital portal (www.gafi.gov.eg) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry's Commercial Registry (al-Sijill al-Tijari)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in the Arabic language as the primary corporate denomination. A transliterated Latin-script trading name may be added for foreign business purposes but is not the legally operative name. The Arabic name must not be identical or phonetically similar to an existing registered name; must not mislead the public as to the object of the company; must not violate public order, ethics, or the State's religious sensitivities; and must end with the legal form designator for limited liability companies: 'شركة ذات مسؤولية محدودة' (LLC).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Public or governmental names (e.g., 'Arab Republic of Egypt', 'Ministry', 'Presidency', 'Governorate')
Islamic (without explicit approval of the Ministry of Endowments)
Union (when implying sovereignty or trade union status)
Sports (subject to Ministry of Youth approval)
Media and Press (subject to Supreme Council for Media Regulation approval)
Free Zone (unless approved by GAFI Free Zones Authority)
Misr / Egypt (when used in a way that implies state affiliation, requiring ministerial clearance)
Foreign sovereign names (e.g., United States, Saudi, China) without bilateral governmental authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by GAFI or the Commercial Registry, the applicant shall file a written administrative grievance (tazallum) with the Legal Affairs Committee of GAFI within 15 working days from the date of rejection, attaching the rejection decision, the proposed amended name, and supporting justification. GAFI must resolve the grievance within 30 working days. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may file a further appeal before the Board of Grievances of the Ministry of Trade and Industry, or directly institute an administrative annulment action before the State Council (Mahkamat al-Dawla) within 60 days under the Provisions of Law No. 9 of 2021 concerning arbitration and administrative litigation. A simultaneously submitted list of three alternative names is recommended to avoid procedural delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not Permitted for Manufacturing LLCs — GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and banks require a physical lease agreement (igara) or usufruct/ownership certificate covering the registered premises for the full term of incorporation, evidenced during GAFI's initial validation step and upon Tax Card issuance. A virtual-address arrangement is insufficient for registration, for industrial licensing, or for opening a corporate bank account, unless co-located with a genuine operating facility. For an ISIC 2740 / NAICS 335122 manufacturing operation, the premises must also approximate sufficient area for light-assembly operations on-site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high: GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority (particularly within the first fiscal year following establishment) conduct unannounced physical inspections to verify the existence and actual commercial substance of the registered office. Estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for an LED grow-light manufacturing facility: 45% due to industrial licensing and VAT registration checks; the likelihood increases to 60% if the entity applies for a customs/importer card or free-zone treatment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Laws No. 4 and No. 5 of 2018, Articles 1-11 (formation of limited liability companies), Article 26 (share capital) and Article 29 (managers); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 7, 8 and 24-26 (GAFI One-Stop-Shop incorporation procedure); Executive Regulations of the Investment Law issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2316 of 2017; Commercial Registry provisions of Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop-Shop Department, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'assis al-Sharika wa Nizamuha al-Asasi) submitted with the Commercial Registration Application (Talab Al-Shahr Al-Tijari).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum paid-up share capital for an LLC is EGP 50,000 (approx. USD 1,600). The full capital amount must be subscribed by the founders at signing and paid into a temporary 'blocked' escrow bank account opened in the name of the company-in-formation at a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt. The resulting Initial Bank Deposit Certificate must be produced to the Notary Public and to the Commercial Registry; the blocked funds are released to the operating corporate account only after the Commercial Registration Certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding members, having fully subscribed and deposited the authorized paid-up share capital of EGP 50,000, hereby ratify their respective share subscriptions and approve the allocation of shares set out in Annex A. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is formally adopted at Plot No. [·], Industrial Zone, 10th of Ramadan City, Ash Sharqia Governorate, and that all corporate records and service of process shall be maintained at such address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name 1], Egyptian National ID No. [·], and [Name 2], ID No. [·], are appointed initial directors/managers, with [Name 1] as General Manager, holding office until the first Ordinary General Assembly. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Manager is authorized to execute the commercial registry filings, tax registrations, and related post-incorporation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop-Shop - Company Name Reservation Desk (electronic portal accessible via GAFI e-services at www.gafi.gov.eg or the physical Tashheelat branch).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a request for reservation of the proposed Arabic trade name of the LLC, e.g., 'Horticultural LED Growth Systems LLC', together with an English transliteration and three alternative names. The authority verifies that the name is not identical or deceptively similar to a name already registered in the Commercial Registry and that it does not contain prohibited religious, governmental or political elements. Upon approval, a formal Name Reservation Certificate is issued, valid for 60 calendar days, which serves as the core identity document for the subsequent notarization and registration steps.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI name reservation application form
Passport or Egyptian national ID copies of all founding members
Notarized power of attorney if submission is made by an authorized incorporator
Proposed trade name in Arabic and Latin script with at least three backup alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected due to similarity with an existing registered commercial mark or for containing restricted wording, the applicant may file a written objection with the GAFI naming committee or simply re-apply using a pre-cleared alternative name. The re-application is processed within two further working days without any penalty or impact on other reserved names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority (Al-Shahr Al-Aqari) operating within the GAFI One-Stop-Shop premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Arabic-language incorporation contract and articles of association to the notary. The deed must state the LLC trade name, corporate form, object comprising the manufacture of commercial agricultural full-spectrum LED grow-light fixtures and ancillary activities, registered office address, authorized and paid-up share capital, quotas of each founding member, the initial managers/directors, fiscal year, and duration not exceeding 25 years. All signatories, or their duly authorized representatives, must appear in person before the notary; foreign founders must present certified Arabic translations of passports, and representatives must hold a special or general power of attorney duly legalized by the competent Egyptian consulate or embassy.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate issued in Step 1
Draft incorporation contract and articles of association in Arabic
Certified passport copies and Arabic translations for foreign founding members
Egyptian national ID copies for resident founding members
Valid power of attorney with Arabic translation for all proxy signatories
Proof of legal title to the registered office address (lease contract or ownership certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises corrections to statutory clauses, such as an unlawful object provision, missing minimum capital declaration, or defective quota allocation, the incorporator files a supplementary deed signed by all founding members, and the notary re-issues the instrument. The full corrective cycle is typically completed within five working days from the date of the original notarial query or rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Temporary Escrow Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of 'the proposed LLC - company in formation' and deposit the full minimum paid-up capital of EGP 50,000, or any higher amount determined by the founders, by debit to the subscribers' legitimate banking channels. Instruct the branch to earmark the balance as blocked funds for the formation and to issue an Initial Bank Deposit Certificate in the name of the LLC under formation. The bank is contractually bound to release the deposited amount to the corporate operating account only after presentation of the Commercial Registration Certificate issued in Step 4.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Certificate
Draft incorporation contract in Arabic
Know-Your-Customer and Anti-Money-Laundering documentation for all initial members per Law No. 80 of 2016
Notarized source-of-funds statement or confirmation letter of each subscribing member
Written instruction letter specifying the escrow purpose and release condition
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account or blocks the deposit because of enhanced diligence findings, the applicant may cure by furnishing supplementary KYC records, including an audit report on source of funds, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and corrected legal identification of the subscribers. Re-application to another licensed bank is permitted, and no administrative penalty accrues during the remediation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Issuance of the Company Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry, administered through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized incorporation deed together with the Initial Bank Deposit Certificate, Name Reservation Certificate, registered-office lease, and the standard Commercial Registry application. The Registrar examines the legality of the corporate object, the adequacy of the paid-up capital representation, the fitness of managers, and compliance with Law No. 159 of 1981. Upon approval, the LLC is allotted a Commercial Registry number, entered in the public Commercial Register, and issued the official Extract of Commercial Registration Certificate, which constitutes statutory incorporation and the acquisition of legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract and articles of association (original plus two copies)
Standard Commercial Registry application form for limited liability companies
Initial Bank Deposit Certificate issued in Step 3
Name Reservation Certificate
Copy of the registered-office lease contract or ownership document
Receipt of payment for official fees, stamp duties and notarial treasury dues
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses or suspends registration due to incomplete quota allocation, an unapproved industrial object, or deficient in-kind valuation, the incorporator must file a corrective notarial addendum and resubmit it to the registrar. The correction procedure extends the timeline by a maximum of ten additional calendar days, after which the certificate is issued retroactively to the application date where permitted by practice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Card, VAT, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) local office and the National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax registration form with the ETA branch to obtain the Company Tax Card and Tax Identification Number, and simultaneously register on the ETA electronic portal for VAT at the standard 14% rate with input-VAT recovery. In parallel, register the LLC and its directors/employees with NOSI within 30 days of commencement of activity; obtain the NOSI registration certificate. The tax card remains conditional upon the payment of relevant stamp duties and the production of the Commercial Registry Extract.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Extract Certificate issued in Step 4
Certified copy of the notarized incorporation deed
Tax registration application form (Form 2 for tax card)
VAT registration request form where applicable
Copies of Egyptian national IDs or passports of all shareholders and managers
Commercial lease contract evidencing the registered business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card issuance is delayed by legacy name or address mismatches, the Company may obtain a corrected Commercial Registry Extract within three working days and resubmit it; if NOSI registration is late, the statutory delay fine must be paid and proof of payment submitted to the insurance branch to prevent doubled late-payment penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Gazette Publication of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette Department (Al-Jarida Al-Rasmiya) of the Egyptian Ministry of Justice in coordination with the GAFI One-Stop-Shop.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate, submit a sealed copy of the notarized deed, the Commercial Registry Extract, and an Arabic summary text to the Official Gazette Department for publication. The publication grants erga omnes effect of the incorporation deed against third parties. The Gazette Department issues an official publication receipt bearing the date and volume number, which is thereafter lodged in the GAFI corporate file and the Commercial Registry dossier.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry Extract Certificate
Certified copy of the notarized incorporation deed
Publication request form in Arabic with summary of the deed
Proof of payment of publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette rejects the summary text due to inaccuracies or inconsistencies with the official registry extract, the Company may resubmit a corrected summary accompanied by a fresh Commercial Registry Extract; republication is completed within five working days without impairment of the Company's existing legal personality.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) - Industrial Licensing Center of the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operation License (Rukhsat Tashghil Sina'i) for the manufacturing plant producing commercial agricultural full-spectrum LED grow-light fixtures, issued under the Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Limited Environmental Assessment under Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 202 of 2020. The LED fixture assembly plant qualifies for the EIA Form B (initial environmental screening) route and is exempted from the full 'List A' Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, provided the facility operates within a designated industrial zone and the production line involves solely electronic component assembly, soldering and mechanical fitting without hazardous chemical manufacturing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater pretreated for municipal sewer discharge must comply with the executive limits of Law No. 48 of 1982 and Decree No. 326 of 1995, including pH 6-9.5, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, COD not exceeding 400 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 400 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 50 mg/L, lead not exceeding 0.1 mg/L, and cadmium not exceeding 0.03 mg/L. Atmospheric emissions from lead-free soldering stations must remain below the stack VOC threshold of 100 ppm, particulate matter not exceeding 40 mg/Nm3, and ambient workplace air quality within the Egyptian Standards ES 3-2010 limits for industrial zones. Hazardous electronic waste, spent solder dross and phosphor-dust residue must be stored on impermeable containment for not more than 90 days and transported by an EEAA-licensed waste handler under the Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Al-Himaya Al-Madaniya) verifying automatic fire suppression, emergency egress capacity, fire compartmentalization and storage flammability controls; a Structural Load and Building Compliance Certificate from a licensed engineering consultancy confirmed by the local municipal engineering department for the assembly-line equipment weight and electrical loads; and an Occupational Safety Clearance from the Manpower Inspectorate of the Ministry of Manpower and Immigration under Labour Law No. 12 of 2003, verifying electrical grounding, machine guarding, lockout-tagout procedures, soldering-station ventilation, harmonic lighting workplaces and emergency exit signage. These clearances are mandatory preconditions for the issuance and annual renewal of the IDA Industrial Operation License.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Authority for Taxation (GAT) under the Ministry of Finance of Egypt
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register as non-residents via the e-Tax portal (tax.eg) or in-person at GAT offices. Submit incorporation certificate, commercial register extract, proof of address, and business activity description. Obtain Tax Registration Number (TRN) within 30 days of approval. Annual renewal required for ongoing operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under Egyptian tax law for cross-border payments and instruments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing via GAT portal API. All invoices require digital stamping and clearance. Non-compliance triggers automated penalties and blocking of bank accounts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods exported outside Egypt and certain offshore services. Requires proof that goods leave Egyptian territory and are not re-imported.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims result in 200% penalty on evaded VAT plus interest and full retrospective clawback. Criminal prosecution possible for willful abuse.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) jointly with the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit (EMLCU) and the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a unified, market-determined managed float (fully liberalized since 6 March 2024), with the EGP trading against the USD at consolidated bank-quoted rates. Current-account convertibility is broadly unrestricted for bona fide trade in goods and services; capital-account transactions (foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, profit distribution, dividend repatriation) are permitted but are subject to documentary verification by an Egyptian authorized bank, issuance of internal foreign-exchange declarations, prior corporate and tax clearances, and registration of the investment certificate with GAFI and the CBE. Profit remittance hurdles are materially reduced but a residual USD liquidity risk and the requirement to present a valid tax clearance certificate, audited financial statements, and a board resolution adopting the distribution remain the principal practical impediments. Fully offshore convertibility of EGP is denied; foreign exchange outside licensed banks is prohibited and carries criminal penalties under Law No. 194 of 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE regulatory instructions (as applied subsequent to the March 2024 unification of the exchange rate), 100% of export proceeds arising from the manufacture of horticultural LED grow-light fixtures must be repatriated into Egypt through a licensed bank and credited to the exporter's designated export-receipt account; no percentage is permitted to be retained offshore. The statutory surrender window is generally 90 days from the bill-of-lading or airway-bill date; extensions up to 360 days may be granted by the exporter's bank on documented commercial terms (deferred payment letters of credit or open-account terms). Proceeds received in a foreign currency may be (i) converted into EGP at prevailing interbank rates, or (ii) held in a foreign-currency account, but the exporter must present the customs export declaration, shipping documents, and CBE form when surrendering. Failure to repatriate within the approved period exposes the entity to non-tariff penalties, bank de-risking, and loss of access to foreign-currency facilities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / FX Trade Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: QNB ALAHLI (Qatar National Bank Al Ahli)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Digital cross-border EMIs (including Airwallex and similar platforms) are not independently licensed in Egypt as banks or payment institutions. They may function only as non-resident invoicing and payout service providers through CBE-licensed sponsor banks or as collection-side FX aggregation tools for receivables received abroad; the in-country payroll, statutory VAT/Tax Payment, social insurance contributions, and export-proceeds surrender obligations must be discharged through a domestic Egyptian bank account. No EMI may open a direct local account in EGP or process CBE-regulated inward remittances without a licensed Egyptian banking partner, and the CBE's Retail Payment Services and Electronic Money Regulations (issued under Law No. 194 of 2020) impose licensing prerequisites for payment initiation, account information, and digital wallet services.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owners and at least one authorized signing director is effectively mandatory under EMLCU's Customer Due Diligence directives. A face-to-face identification meeting must be conducted either (i) by a bank compliance officer at the branch in Egypt, or (ii) through a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney combined with video-identification where the bank's compliance committee accepts it; in practice most Egyptian hierarchy-1 banks require in-branch physical attendance of the foreign UBO and the appointed EG resident manager. Remote account opening is not recognized as standard; the CBE mandate includes live interview of the UBO, verification of original corporate documents, board resolutions, and a bank-specific legal opinion on the borrowing and signing authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification gap where an indirect foreign shareholder exercises control through a discretionary trust or holding chain exceeding 25%
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register, trust deed or ownership cascade chart certified by the Egyptian notary, valid passports and Egyptian national ID copies, corporate registry extracts from each layer, source-of-wealth declaration, and a legal opinion confirming the non-PEP, non-sanctioned status of all controlling parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth insufficiency for the initial capital injection through SWIFT wire
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the foreign parent for the last 3 years, personal bank reference letters, sale-and-purchase or dividend distribution documentation supporting the wired funds, tax receipts, and a forward-looking business plan showing justified working-capital deployment in the Egyptian horticultural LED manufacturing facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-scope mismatch: declared ISIC 2740 LED manufacturing activity versus imported finished-goods trading profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industrial registry certificate low-risk manufacturing designation, factory lease or title deed, machinery import invoices, Environmental/health and safety approval, electricity utility bills, job-creation payroll records, and product origin certification demonstrating in-country assembly of the LED grow-light units.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list hits or adverse-medial reporting on a beneficial owner or shipping counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN/EU/OFAC/UK-HMT full sanctions screening result sheets, passport and nationality documentation, commercial registry background, written explanation from the compliance officer, and transaction-level justification evidencing no nexus to sanctioned jurisdictions or military-grade buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of a shareholder or board member
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Declared PEP questionnaire, independent wealth proof based on audited results and salary/investment records, notarized undertaking on use of funds, enhanced due diligence report from a licensed external consultant, and confirmation of nil adverse legal proceedings in Egyptian courts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-financing red flag: entrusted SWIFT payments to third-party suppliers without an underlying bill-of-lading trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders, proforma invoices, signed sales contracts, shipping documents (B/L, AWB), Egypt customs import declarations, transfer-of-title insurance, and bank-certified historical trade files from the GCC or EU distribution counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign capital (equity or shareholder loan) must be wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the Egyptian bank's foreign-currency account, denominated ordinarily in USD or EUR, with the beneficiary account classified under the capital-escrow or foreign-investment account scheme. The remittance must carry the sender's bank reference with the purpose-of-payment field stating 'Capital Contribution / Investment Capital' or 'Shareholder Loan', and the Egyptian receiving bank requires a post-receipt inward-transfer declaration, a board resolution of the Egyptian LLC subscribing the shares, the GAFI investment registration certificate or free-zone license, the company's Commercial Registry (CR) extract, Tax Card, and a CBE exchange-control form executed by the authorized bank officer. For shareholder loans, the bank will additionally require a signed shareholder loan agreement with an arm's-length interest rate, a repayment schedule, and confirmation that the loan is subordinated to the bank's own facilities where credit exposure is sought. Funds must not be commingled with operational collections prior to conversion into EGP.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for outbound disbursements (component imports and payments to foreign distribution partners) are executed through (i) SWIFT MT103 straight transfer for open-account or advance payments, provided full underlying trade documentation and a CBE import-form are submitted, (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued in favor of foreign suppliers (SWIFT MT700), (iii) documentary collections (D/P and D/A), and (iv) low-value global payouts via licensed sponsor-bank-integrated fintech rails such as Airwallex exclusively for foreign currency balances held offshore and not requiring EGP conversion. For imports above the CBE threshold, the importer bank must verify the purchase order, proforma invoice, pricing benchmark, shipping terms, and customs declaration; advance payments exceeding statutory percentages require enhanced due diligence and sometimes bank-level authorization. All outbound foreign-currency disbursements must be funded from the company's foreign-currency operational account or through conversion of EGP at the unified interbank rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore outright EGP/USD forward contracts executed with an Egyptian authorized bank covering genuine trade or investment exposure
FX swaps (swap of EGP against USD/EUR principal with simultaneous spot and forward legs) authorized by the CBE through licensed dealer banks
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for matched shareholder-loan or trade-finance liabilities
Non-deliverable offshore forwards (NDF) referencing EGP traded abroad but used by the non-resident shareholder as a macro-hedge; direct resident participation is not recognized under CBE rules
Collared or plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options where the CBE-authorized instructing bank permits them for trade hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Annual Renewal (Tajdeed Al-Sijill Al-Tijari)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office / GAFI under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - January 31 of each calendar year, irrespective of incorporation anniversary; e-filing available via GAFI portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal to February 28 incurs a fixed EGP 100 fine; renewal after February 28 triggers additional administrative penalties, suspension of the commercial register card, and eventual administrative strike-off of the LLC's registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form No. 19) with Audited Financial Statements Attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end; for a December year-end LLC, filing is due on or before April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay surcharge of 2% of unpaid corporate tax (capped at 100%), fixed late-filing fines under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, enforced collections, and suspension of the tax card

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Partners' (Shareholders') Meeting Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI company file (held on-site and available for inspection); copy submitted to ETA with Form No. 19
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Statutory approval within six months of the fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year LLC); ETA attachment due by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal warning and fines under Companies Law 159/1981 for failure to prepare or approve audited annual accounts; an auditor's qualified opinion is treated by ETA as a tax irregularity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing at incorporation; update within 30 days of any ownership change; annual re-confirmation made during the January commercial-register renewal window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 20,000 - 80,000 for missing, outdated, or inaccurate UBO records (Law 185/2020 amendments); GAFI may additionally suspend corporate transactions until rectification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tax Card Validity Maintenance and Annual ETA Status Reaffirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously maintained; reaffirmed upon the April 30 corporate income tax filing and completion of annual withholding reconciliations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expired or suspended tax card blocks customs clearance, public tender participation, and corporate banking transactions; persistent non-compliance leads to administrative revocation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An LLC with issued capital of EGP 250,000 or more must appoint an independent certified auditor; a lower-capital LLC may elect a controller unless shareholders holding at least 10% of capital demand a full auditor; ETA nonetheless requires audited balance sheet and income statement to accompany the corporate tax return, and the LED manufacturing inventory activity effectively mandates an external audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), the IFRS-converged local GAAP issued by the Ministry of Investment; full IFRS is permitted for listed and significant entities; mandatory ETA e-invoicing and e-receipts require system-integrated accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a beneficial ownership register at its head office and file or update UBO data with GAFI within 30 days of any shareholding or control change; an annual re-confirmation is submitted during the January commercial-register renewal, certifying current UBOs (natural persons holding 25% or more of capital, voting rights, or effective control) and attaching the partners' approval.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managers and Directors (Quayd Al-Mudireen)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Five-year income tax holiday for qualifying new industrial projects under Investment Law No. 96/2015 in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) or less-developed governorates; eligible LED horticultural fixture manufacturing may also access preferential import duty treatment on capital equipment under the Customs Law; reinvested profits used to acquire additional fixed assets are deductible against taxable income subject to ETA conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 35 (Model 35) and estimated return Form No. 34, submitted electronically via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-filing portal at www.eta.gov.eg (also mirrored on the integrated e-tax platform under Law No. 1 of 2022 on Unified Tax Procedures).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return Form No. 35 is due within four months following the end of the tax year (fiscal year). Quarterly estimated returns Form No. 34, together with advance tax payments, are due within one month after the close of each of the first three quarters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, head office address, activity code (ISIC 2740 – Manufacture of electric lighting equipment), and designated tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ETA-issued nine-digit tax registration number for the Egyptian LLC; for a foreign parent branch filing, indicate the Egyptian branch registration and parent foreign tax ID in the remarks field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period subject to the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian fiscal year end; if the ultimate parent consolidates on a different year-end, keep the same period as previously approved by the ETA to preserve carryforward consistency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross sales and services revenue arising from Egyptian-source activities, including local sales of horticultural LED grow lights and export sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report in EGP using the official Central Bank of Egypt exchange rate at transaction date; attach a schedule reconciling foreign currency export proceeds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct materials, direct labor, and production overheads attributable to LED fixture manufacturing, supported by the audited financial statements and inventory count records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany imports of parts must be valued at arm's length; attach transfer pricing documentation if any related-party purchases exceed EGP 15 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative, selling, and general expenses with Egyptian tax invoice support; entertainment, donations, and certain travel costs are subject to statutory deduction caps (e.g., 50% disallowance for entertainment).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-service charges (technical fees, management fees) must be backed by withholding tax certificates; taxpayers must add back undeclared non-deductible items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net result after adjustments for disallowable expenses, exempt income, and prior-period corrections per the ETA inspection standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers must include Egyptian-source turnover attributable to a permanent establishment; artificially shifting profit to foreign affiliates will be recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses incurred in prior years and utilized against current-year taxable income, limited to a maximum five-year carryforward from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the ETA-approved loss utilization computation; losses of a foreign jurisdiction cannot be offset against Egyptian-source income unless supported by a valid tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Computed Tax at Statutory Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on the net taxable income at 22.5%, before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applying treaty-reduced rates is not permitted at this box; treaty relief is reflected only after the ETA approves the DTA application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 – Credits, Advance Payments, and WHT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments (Form 34), foreign tax credits within treaty limits, and Egyptian withholding tax already borne on interest, dividends, or contractor payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach ETA receipts for each advance payment and WHT certificates; foreign tax credits require a valid Tax Residency Certificate and treaty article completion form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 – Net Tax Due or Refund Claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive balance to be paid or negative balance to be refunded, including the delay surcharge calculation if the deadline was missed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxpayers must settle any remaining payable through the e-collection bank network or the ETA treasury account and file the payment method declaration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly delay surcharge of 2% of the outstanding tax per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100% of the assessed tax; a fixed administrative fine for non-filing ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000 under Law No. 1 of 2022. Late payment: additional 2% per month surcharge plus statutory interest. Failure to keep books: up to EGP 50,000 administrative penalty. Directors will be summoned personally if the company remains in default after the inspection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 58); the distributing Egyptian LLC must withhold the 10% dividend distribution tax from amounts payable to both resident and non-resident shareholders, with no exemption for non-residents absent a ratified tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder must submit to the Egyptian LLC, no later than 30 days before the dividend payment date: (i) an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority for the relevant calendar year, (ii) a fully completed DTA relief application form (ETA Form - Treaty Benefit Claim), (iii) beneficial ownership statement confirming the shareholder receives the dividend for its own account, and (iv) a certificate of incorporation. The LLC files the relief application with the ETA through the unified e-portal; the ETA reviews and issues an official approval ruling. Only upon ETA approval may the reduced treaty rate be applied; absent approval, the statutory 10% must be withheld and remitted within 15 days of distribution. The approved relief must be renewed annually and on any material change of ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under Law No. 91 of 2005: interest paid to non-residents at 20%, royalties for IP/licensing at 20%, and payments for certain technical services at 20%. Under Egypt's DTA network, reduced rates commonly range from 5% to 15% for interest and 10% to 15% for royalties, depending on the counterparty treaty (e.g., OECD-aligned treaties). Treaty relief follows the same TRC and beneficial-ownership procedure described above. Interest on export financing loans from foreign banks may be exempt if financing is denominated in foreign currency and approved by the Central Bank of Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 15 million. Master File: mandatory where total related-party transactions exceed EGP 30 million or the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds EGP 100 million per fiscal year. Country-by-Country Report (CbCR): required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EGP 18 billion, aligned with the OECD's EUR 750 million filing threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply standalone Economic Substance Regulations modeled on the UAE/IFC regime; however, the ETA enforces an equivalent standard through the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR), the beneficial ownership requirement under tax treaty provisions, and the arm's length principle under Article 30 of Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 1 of 2022. A manufacturing LLC claiming the SCZone tax holiday or treaty benefits must maintain actual business premises in the zone, employ the relevant workforce, undertake real production of horticultural LED fixtures, and retain full records of its economic activities. Transactions with a related party that has no substantive business are disregarded, and the associated income is re-attributed to the Egyptian taxpayer with late-payment surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating gross revenues from horticultural LED light exports, issuing or using fake tax invoices for phantom imports of components, or recording fictitious operating expenses to reduce taxable income below EGP 22.5% effective taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Article 133 of Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 1 of 2022: imprisonment for a term of up to five years and/or a fine of up to EGP 1,000,000; civil assessment of the full evaded tax plus a 2% monthly delay surcharge capped at 100% of the tax; confiscation of falsified documents and assets derived from the evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign knowingly false returns or direct book-keeping manipulation become jointly and severally liable for the civil tax debt, face criminal conviction, a travel ban, and freezing of personal bank accounts, and may be barred from serving on any Egyptian company board for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Egyptian LLC as a letterbox entity without manufacturing premises, employees, or actual production of LED grow lights while claiming the Investment Law tax holiday, treaty reduced withholding rates, or tax-free profit repatriation; shuffling purchase and sales invoices through Egypt without physical goods movement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA disregards the entity for tax purposes; denial of all tax holidays and treaty benefits; re-assessment on a deemed profit basis at 22.5% with 2% monthly delay surcharge; potential administrative strike-off from the Commercial Register; referral to the Public Prosecutor for operating a sham company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil allows the ETA and creditors to attach the directors' personal assets; the Anti-Money Laundering Unit may impose travel bans and asset freezes for the duration of the criminal investigation; additional liability for fraud against minority shareholders and foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling horticultural LED grow lights to a related party in a zero-tax jurisdiction at a deliberately deflated gross margin, paying inflated royalties to a connected IP holder for generic LED driver technology, or charging excessive management fees from a parent company without evidence of services received.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA transfer pricing adjustment under the arm's length principle using CUP/TNMM, involuntary assessment of additional taxable income at 22.5%, application of a 2% monthly delay surcharge, and a documentation penalty of up to 1% of the relevant related-party transaction value for failure to produce a Local/Master File; repeat offenders face criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the non-arm's length pricing are jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties; travel bans are routinely applied when the ETA issues a criminal tax evasion referral; professional director disqualification may be imposed by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit Dividend / Royalty / Interest WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without deducting the 10% statutory tax, paying royalty or interest invoices without the 20% WHT, or remitting withheld amounts late to the Treasury despite the ETA receipts showing payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The un-withheld tax is immediately assessed against the distributing entity; a monthly delay surcharge of 2% on the un-remitted WHT (capped at 100%) and an additional administrative fine under Law No. 1 of 2022 ranging from EGP 20,000 to EGP 100,000; the ETA may also charge the entire obligation against the company's bank accounts by executive order without a court judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Withheld taxes retain a public-fund character; directors who divert or fail to remit them are personally liable for the full amount and may be prosecuted for misuse of public funds, leading to imprisonment, seizure of personal assets, and a strict travel ban pending full repayment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Breach / Structuring of Export Proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving international wire transfers from horticultural LED buyers through personal or shell intermediary accounts in Dubai, Hong Kong, or the United Kingdom; splitting payments into amounts below AED/USD reporting thresholds to evade the Egyptian Currency and AML controls; failing to maintain the underlying purchase orders, bills of lading, and customs declarations for the LED fixtures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering felony under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended): imprisonment for 3 to 7 years and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000; seizure of all funds and assets related to the offense; mandatory license revocation for the company; possible blacklisting by Egyptian banks and loss of access to the SWIFT system in Egypt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who opened or controlled the foreign shell accounts are criminally liable as principals; they face cumulative sentences, full confiscation of personal and corporate assets, automatic passport revocation, and an international travel ban; extradition may be requested from the foreign jurisdiction hosting the intermediary account.
